name: Oracle
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Oracle has converted itself into the largest external AI-compute landlord on earth — remaining performance obligations of $638B (+363%) at fiscal year-end May 2026, roughly half of it attributed by press reporting to a single ~$300B five-year OpenAI contract starting 2027 — and is funding the buildout with debt and equity at a scale ($43B debt plus $5B equity raised in FY2026, ~$40B more planned, free cash flow negative $23.7B) that made its credit default swaps a market-wide barometer for AI-capex risk. BACKGROUND: Founded 1977; database and SaaS incumbent; fiscal year ends May 31. FY2026 revenue $67.4B (+17%), with OCI infrastructure revenue $18.1B (+77%) on a company-published trajectory to $144B by FY2030. Dual-CEO structure since September 2025 (Clay Magouyrk and Mike Sicilia); Safra Catz moved to executive vice chair; new CFO Hilary Maxson arrived from Schneider Electric with an AES energy background. Oracle is the compute landlord for five named US Stargate campuses and discloses per-site power strategy in unusual detail.
ecosystemRole: We assess Oracle as the demand-side account with the most explicit power-procurement story in this file: it does not just buy data centers, it publishes how each campus is powered — a genset microgrid at Shackelford (115 MW already live), a Bloom Energy fuel-cell microgrid at Doña Ana (up to 2.45 GW earmarked, replacing planned gas turbines and diesel), GE Vernova turbines plus grid at Abilene, DTE grid plus new battery storage at Saline Township, and ~70% renewables-plus-battery at Port Washington. Basis: Oracle's own data-center hub pages and the January 2026 'we pay our own way on energy' policy post. For power and BESS vendors, Oracle campuses are the single richest observable menu of behind-the-fence power choices — and its OpenAI concentration makes it the sector's counterparty-risk bellwether.

productsAndServices.name: OCI AI infrastructure (Superclusters, Zettascale10)
productsAndServices.description: GPU superclusters up to 131,072 NVIDIA B200 or >100,000 GB200 superchips per cluster; OCI Zettascale10 (announced October 2025) scales to 800,000 NVIDIA GPUs and 16 zettaFLOPS peak at multi-gigawatt power, with GPUs clustered within a two-kilometer radius and Oracle's Acceleron RoCE networking (400G/800G). Launch partner for AMD Instinct MI450 superclusters (initial 50,000 GPUs from Q3 CY2026 on Helios racks).
productsAndServices.positioning: A ~3-4% share cloud by general-purpose measures (Synergy-derived), but the #1 external AI-compute landlord — competing with CoreWeave-class neoclouds for frontier-lab workloads more than with AWS/Azure/GCP platform businesses.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Multi-year committed cloud contracts; increasingly structured with customer GPU prepayment or customer-supplied GPUs ($75B of RPO).
targetSegments: Frontier AI labs (OpenAI, Meta, NVIDIA, xAI commitments named)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Company-published OCI revenue plan: $18B (FY2026) → $32B → $73B → $114B → $144B (FY2030). Zettascale10 availability 2H CY2026.

productsAndServices.name: Stargate campus buildout (compute landlord role)
productsAndServices.description: Oracle-partnered Stargate sites: Abilene TX (flagship — 8 buildings, 1,100 acres; ~42% of capacity delivered as of June 2026; ~0.3 GW live per independent tracking, building to 1.2 GW by Q4 2026), Shackelford County TX (2.0 GW, off-grid genset microgrid, delivery from 1H 2027), Doña Ana County NM (2.2 GW, Bloom fuel-cell microgrids), Port Washington WI (1.3 GW with Vantage, ~70% zero-emission), Saline Township MI (1.4 GW, DTE grid + BESS, Related Digital/Blackstone/PIMCO financing). Oracle owns the hardware at all US Stargate sites except the two SoftBank-led ones.
productsAndServices.positioning: Operational responsibility sits with OpenAI, build execution with developers (Crusoe, Vantage, STACK, Related), power with utilities and on-site vendors — Oracle is the contracting hub that turns OpenAI demand into physical campuses.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term cloud contracts backed by project-financed campuses (~$38B of adjacent Vantage debt reported).
productsAndServices.roadmap: ~7 GW planned across announced sites toward the $500B/10 GW Stargate envelope; independent tracking shows ~0.3 GW operational today — the delivery gap is the central execution question.

productsAndServices.name: Database, applications & multicloud core
productsAndServices.description: The legacy franchise: Oracle Database (MultiCloud AI Database growing 404-531% off a small base as it deploys inside AWS/Azure/GCP datacenters), Fusion/NetSuite SaaS ($15.9B FY2026, +11%), and 211 live-and-planned cloud regions. This ~70%-gross-margin business funds and collateralizes the AI infrastructure expansion.
productsAndServices.positioning: The cash cow whose margin profile the AI buildout dilutes — leaked internals put GPU-rental gross margins at ~14-16% versus ~70% for the legacy stack.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Enterprise licensing, SaaS subscriptions, multicloud partnerships.
productsAndServices.roadmap: FY2027 guidance ~$90B total revenue (+27-29%) with cloud growing 57-64%; CFO guided gross margin to step down on data-center ramp mix.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2026 results: RPO $638B (+363%), revenue $67.4B (+17%), FCF -$23.7B; stock fell ~10% on ~$40B more planned financing and a guided gross-margin step-down
recentDevelopments.read: The definitive statement of the model: backlog and capex both compounding, funded externally. $75B of RPO now comes from GPU-prepayment or customer-supplied-GPU structures — a disclosure that blurs what 'backlog' means.

recentDevelopments.headline: Project Jupiter (Doña Ana County, NM) to be powered by Bloom Energy fuel cells — up to 2.45 GW, replacing previously planned gas turbines and diesel gensets
recentDevelopments.read: The largest fuel-cell commitment in data-center history, and the clearest evidence Oracle treats power architecture as a per-site competitive decision.

recentDevelopments.headline: Record-demand ~$25B investment-grade bond plus ~$25B equity-linked plan (including a $20B at-the-market program); CDS spreads collapsed from 18-year highs
recentDevelopments.read: The equity component calmed a credit market that had S&P at BBB- (one notch above junk) and CDS above 200bp — the financing plan, not the earnings, restored confidence.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'We pay our own way on energy' policy post: on-site generation or Oracle-funded grid upgrades, no ratepayer pass-through, closed-loop non-evaporative cooling standard
recentDevelopments.read: A direct response to the utility-cost-shifting backlash — and a de facto procurement spec for power vendors bidding Oracle campuses.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 FY2026: RPO $523B (+438%) with new Meta and NVIDIA commitments — but ~$12B quarterly capex and ~$10B FCF loss triggered a ~$67B one-day market-cap loss
recentDevelopments.read: The quarter that established the pattern: backlog beats are no longer enough; the market trades the capex and financing lines.

recentDevelopments.headline: OCI Zettascale10 unveiled: up to 800,000 NVIDIA GPUs, 16 zettaFLOPS, multi-gigawatt clusters within a 2 km radius; AMD MI450 launch partnership (50,000 GPUs from Q3 CY2026)
recentDevelopments.read: The Abilene fabric productized — and the industry's most concrete disclosure of what 'multi-gigawatt AI cluster' means physically.

recentDevelopments.headline: Five new Stargate sites announced with OpenAI/SoftBank — Stargate reaches ~7 GW planned, >$400B over three years
recentDevelopments.read: Oracle-partnered sites (Shackelford, Doña Ana, Wisconsin) formalized the multi-campus landlord role beyond Abilene.

recentDevelopments.headline: Dual-CEO structure: Clay Magouyrk (OCI) and Mike Sicilia (Industries) promoted; Safra Catz to executive vice chair
recentDevelopments.read: Leadership reorganized around the AI-infrastructure and applications split; the OCI engineer now co-runs the company.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q1 FY2026: RPO $455B (+359%) — stock rose 30-36% in a day despite missing both revenue and EPS consensus
recentDevelopments.read: The RPO shock that repriced the company; the WSJ-reported ~$300B OpenAI contract is the bulk of it.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Oracle's AI story is a concentrated landlord bet, not broad cloud share gain. Basis: ~3-4% general cloud share (Synergy-derived) against $638B RPO of which roughly half is press-attributed to OpenAI; analysts openly handicap collectability ('very high uncertainty this customer will be able to pay' — DA Davidson), and Oracle has never disclosed the customer split.

(High confidence) We assess the buildout is structurally debt-and-equity funded with thin near-term economics. Basis: FCF -$23.7B in FY2026, ~$130B total debt, S&P at BBB- with a forecast FY2027 FCF deficit of ~$42B, and leaked internals (The Information) showing ~14-16% gross margins on GPU rentals versus ~70% legacy — the CFO's own FY2027 gross-margin step-down guidance corroborates the direction.

(High confidence) We assess Oracle's per-site power diversity is deliberate procurement strategy, not improvisation — and the best public map of behind-the-fence options. Basis: five simultaneously active but different architectures (gensets, fuel cells, turbines+grid, utility+BESS, renewables+BESS) with the January 2026 policy post codifying self-funded energy as doctrine.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the RPO number overstates firm demand. Basis: $75B is GPU-prepayment/customer-supplied structures; the Abilene expansion to 2.1 GW was reversed per independent tracking; and ~0.3 GW operational versus >9 GW projected by 2029 leaves conversion overwhelmingly in front of, not behind, the company.

(Low confidence) We assess the Abilene permitting controversy (turbines authorized via minor 'permit by rule' pathways; community-notification failures documented by Floodlight and the Texas Tribune) is a latent regulatory and reputational exposure for the whole behind-the-fence generation model, not just Oracle. Basis: press investigation only; no enforcement action reported to date.

periods.commentary: Backlog quadrupled while free cash flow went deeply negative. Q1's RPO shock added 30-36% in a day; Q2's capex disclosure erased ~$67B of market cap in a day; Q4's financing plans cut ~10%. Oracle became the market's live experiment in debt-funded AI landlording.
